title: tune-nccl-overlap-tp-collectives-async-batching
author: Ravi Patel
description:
Motivation: on multi-GPU tensor-parallel runs we observed suboptimal overlap between communication (NCCL collectives) and kernel compute when using the default stream scheduling. This PR improves NCCL stream/priority assignment, introduces an async-collective wrapper that performs non-blocking progress and stream-aware synchronization, and updates the continuous batcher + KV-cache prefetch to issue prefetches on lower-priority comm streams. The goal is to increase throughput on 8+ GPU boxes with minimal latency regression and no API changes.

What this change does: - Add a small async collective abstraction (redwood/runtime/tensor_parallel/async_collective.{h,cpp}) that posts NCCL collectives on dedicated comm streams and exposes a future-like handle for later synchronization. The implementation uses CUDA events to synchronize without blocking the compute stream. - Tune NCCL stream priorities and ordering in nccl_scheduler.cpp: compute kernels are scheduled on high-priority streams, collectives on medium/low priority streams to maximize overlap; we also refine stream assignment per-rank for intra-node vs inter-node cases. - KV-cache prefetch is changed to issue non-blocking sends/recvs on comm streams and prefetch proactively for the next token window during continuous batching. - Continuous batcher updated to prefer issuing kernel launches on compute streams and to allow outstanding async collectives up to a configurable watermark. - Added end-to-end perf test and dashboards (redwood/tests/perf/tp_collectives_perf.py and redwood/docs/perf/tp_nccl_tuning.md).

Results: internal perf-canary on 8xA100/P4d-equivalent hardware shows +12-18% throughput for typical chat workloads (seq_len 512, batch 8) and 8-12% improvement on longer sequences. 99th percentile tail latency is unchanged within noise. Memory overhead is +~1%.

Risks and mitigations: - Potential deadlocks if sync ordering is incorrect: added e2e tests and stress test that exercised various rank/stream interleavings. - Flaky CI on GPU runners: test marked and retried in CI; instrumentation added to help triage.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-2314) - [x] Perf canary executed and numbers attached - [x] Unit and integration tests updated - [x] Backwards-compatible: no public API changes

Related: Linear ENG-2314, ENG-2378. Jira SUP-412 for customer-reported regression that motivated additional KV-cache prefetching work.
